fields.situation: Bed 4, a baby born at 34 weeks, now 6 days old, arrived on 7 West by elevator in a transport incubator. He is stable in the incubator on room air.
fields.background: Printed NICU handoff card (printed at hurricane warning, updated 08:15): Preterm, 34 weeks, day of life 6. ALLERGY: vancomycin (red-man reaction). PIV in the left hand with D10W maintenance fluids. Blood culture drawn 03:10 for temperature instability and is PENDING. Ampicillin started 03:40; next antibiotic dose due 11:00. Feeds every 3 hours, next feed 07:00.
fields.assessment: Stable in the incubator on room air, IV fluids running through the PIV.
fields.readBack: Got it. Read-back: Bed 4, room air, PIV fluids, feed at 10:00, no allergies, nothing pending. Okay to sign?

instructorNote: This inject tests the handoff under NUR-EM-07 step 5. The read-back says "no allergies, nothing pending", but the card shows a vancomycin allergy, a blood culture drawn at 03:10 that is still pending and an antibiotic due at 08:00. The NICU Charge Nurse should stop the signature, have the read-back done again in full (diagnosis, code status, allergies, infusions, next medication, pending tests) and then have the receiving nurse confirm arrival on the tracking board. If the error is missed, carry it into Phase 4: the 11:00 antibiotic order flags on 7 West and the culture comes back positive.
